Updated Met Office guidance ahead of peak heating will be the key near-term catalyst for any shifts in trader positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ensemble forecasts from major models show Milan’s August 15 high temperature most likely reaching 34–35 °C under a persistent high-pressure ridge and light southerly flow, with limited cloud cover and urban heat-island effects boosting daytime maxima. Recent runs exhibit a narrow spread centered near these values, reflecting typical late-summer variability and the influence of soil moisture and boundary-layer mixing. Traders price 34 °C and 35 °C nearly equally because small shifts in wind speed or afternoon convection could tip the official reading either way, while probabilities drop sharply outside this narrow band given the current synoptic setup and climatological precedent for early-August heat in the Po Valley.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon activity over Luzon continues to shape Manila’s near-term temperature outlook, with PAGASA forecasts indicating mostly cloudy skies, scattered thunderstorms, and highs near 30–33°C through August 15. Enhanced cloud cover and frequent convective rainfall limit surface heating by reducing incoming solar radiation while high humidity and urban heat-island effects sustain warmth overnight. The closely matched market probabilities for 31°C and 32°C reflect uncertainty in afternoon thunderstorm timing and intensity, which can suppress peak readings by 1–2°C on any given day. Distant tropical systems add further variability to steering patterns and moisture influx, keeping 33°C or higher less likely absent a brief clearing trend. Updated PAGASA model runs and satellite observations over the next 48 hours will refine these resolution thresholds.
